page: Microsoft Azure E2a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. It includes 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 51 GB disk, and there are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the E2a_v4 delivers modest processing capabilities. Multi-core performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the bottom 10% tier, reflecting the constraints of its dual-vCPU configuration. Single-core performance is more competitive, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks achieving average ratings. Memory performance is mixed; while the Passmark memory score is average, uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths are weak, and small-block cached read bandwidth is poor. Database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving also rank in the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile, the E2a_v4 offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. The generous 16.0 GB RAM allocation relative to its 2 vCPUs makes it suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, or lightweight enterprise applications with low CPU utilization. However, the poor multi-core scaling and low database transaction benchmarks suggest it is not suited for high-throughput production databases, heavy compilation, or real-time data processing.
description: The Microsoft Azure E2a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads), 16.0 GB of RAM, and 51 GB of local storage, with no GPU. This configuration yields a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Performance benchmarks show average single-core and text-processing capabilities, but poor multi-core, database, and web-serving throughput. Consequently, the E2a_v4 is a cost-effective option for memory-bound, low-CPU workloads such as small caching layers, lightweight enterprise applications, and basic memory-intensive development environments, while remaining less suitable for compute-heavy or high-transaction database tasks.
